root_cause.text: In the NETDEV_REGISTER notification handlers of nft_chain_filter.c and nf_tables_api.c, the duplicate device registration check incorrectly required the `changename` flag to be true when `ops` was already set, allowing a second registration attempt when `changename` was false and the hook was already registered.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (!match || (changename && ops))` to `if (!match || ops)` in both handlers, removing the `changename` dependency so that any existing non-null `ops` prevents duplicate registration. The commit message explicitly states that duplicate device registration must be avoided because the device may already have been added by `nft_netdev_hook_alloc()` when creating the hook.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect condition to prevent duplicate hook registration and memory leak when a flowtable hook already exists.
intent_record.what: Removed the 'changename' check from the condition in the NETDEV_REGISTER case of nft_flowtable_event, so the condition is now 'if (!match || ops)' instead of 'if (!match || (changename && ops))'.
intent_record.how: For NETDEV_REGISTER events, the code now skips hook ops allocation when ops is already non-null, regardless of whether the device name changed (changename). Previously it would only skip if both changename and ops were true, allowing potential duplicate allocation and memory leak when changename was false but ops was already set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential duplicate chain registration on netdev register event by skipping when ops already assigned, regardless of changename flag.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_REGISTER case of nft_netdev_event, the condition for skipping registration was changed from '!match || (changename && ops)' to '!match || ops', removing the dependency on changename.
intent_record.how: Previously, the code would skip registration only if both changename was true and ops was non-NULL. Now it skips registration whenever ops is non-NULL, regardless of changename. This prevents possible duplicate allocation and assignment of basechain ops when ops already exists but changename is false.
